sections.title: Listening. Listen to five short recordings about weather and nature. Choose the correct answers.
sections.script:
One.
Good morning. Today will be dry and sunny in the south, but in the north there will be heavy snow this afternoon, so please drive carefully.
Two.
After the earthquake, most buildings in the town were fine. The biggest problem was the water — the pipes broke and people had no clean water for three days.
Three.
I usually paint in the garden, but at the moment it's far too windy. Yesterday my painting flew over the fence into my neighbour's garden!
Four.
I couldn't sleep last night. It wasn't the heat — it was the thunder. It was so loud that the windows were shaking.
Five.
Our holiday was lovely, although the weather was a bit disappointing. It was cloudy almost every day, but at least it didn't rain.

sections.title: H. Read the text. Are the sentences true or false?
sections.passage:
Uzbekistan has a continental climate: summers are long, hot and dry, and winters can be surprisingly cold. In July, temperatures in Termez sometimes reach 45°C, while in January the mountains near Tashkent can be −20°C.

Spring is the shortest and the most beautiful season. For a few weeks the hills turn green and red with tulips, and families go on picnics. But spring also brings sudden storms, and in the mountain valleys heavy rain can cause mudslides.

The biggest environmental problem in the region is water. The Aral Sea was once the fourth largest lake in the world, but it lost most of its water in the 20th century because rivers were used for cotton farms. Today, scientists and local people are planting trees on the old sea bed to stop the dust storms.

items.q: Summers in Uzbekistan are usually wet.
It can be −20°C in the mountains near Tashkent.
Spring is the longest season.
Heavy rain in spring can cause mudslides.
People are planting trees on the old bed of the Aral Sea.
